```json
{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "The NodeJS SDK (fabric-sdk-node) is used as the reference for the Java and Python SDK API surface and feature parity.",
    "Java SDK will be implemented as a thin gRPC client on top of the existing Fabric protos (orderer, peer, event, discovery), following the same lifecycle/identity/chaincode abstractions as fabric-sdk-node.",
    "Python SDK will be implemented using the official `grpcio` library, mirroring the same abstractions; the existing python `fabric-sdk-py` is taken as the starting point to be brought to feature parity.",
    "For U3, pre-built user chaincode is delivered as OCI/Docker images built by the chaincode owner; the peer is extended to skip the local build step when an image reference is supplied in the chaincode deployment spec.",
    "For U3, multi-arch images (linux/amd64, linux/s390x, linux/ppc64le, linux/arm64) are built via Docker buildx and published to a registry; the deployment spec carries the image identifier.",
    "For U4, the enhanced VSCC log/event payload is added inside the existing VSCC ValidateTx path in core/committer/txvalidator; no policy-evaluation algorithm changes are made.",
    "For U5, Go-based tools (configtxgen, fabric-chaintool, fabric-ca-client, cryptogen, etc.) are cross-compiled via the existing Makefile; release artifacts are packaged and hosted alongside Fabric releases.",
    "For U6, the certificate-pinning feature is implemented as an Auth Handler (per the FAB-4207 reference) that validates endorser certs against an organization-controlled fingerprint list fetched at endorsement time.",
    "For U6, the fingerprint list is hosted at an organization-controlled HTTP endpoint configured in the channel config; an alternative key-signed in-channel fingerprint list is not pursued in this increment to keep complexity down.",
    "For U7, testing.html is updated to link to existing READMEs in fabric/test/ rather than authoring new tests; one sample BYFN-style network is referenced.",
    "For U8, a `config_defaults/` directory is created at the repo root containing core.yaml, orderer.yaml, configtx.yaml, and related files with all options populated using the current code defaults; sampleconfig/ is deprecated."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "One work-day equals 8 hours of focused development by a single senior Go/JS/Java/Python developer familiar with Hyperledger Fabric internals.",
    "The two SDKs (Java, Python) are built largely in parallel by the same developer (sequenced, not staffed) so the estimate reflects wall-clock effort of one person.",
    "No new consensus, ordering, or state-DB features are required; existing Fabric binary protocol is reused.",
    "CI/CD and release infrastructure for binary distribution (U5) already exists; the work is limited to wiring up cross-compilation and publishing.",
    "Docker Hub or a similar OCI registry is available and acceptable for distributing pre-built chaincode images (U3).",
    "The certificate-pinning implementation (U6) follows the Auth Handler approach; no changes to the gossip or orderer layers are required.",
    "Documentation work for U7 and U8 is limited to consolidating existing content and adding links/headers; no large new tutorials are written.",
    "An additional 10% effort is included as an 'integration testing & code review' line to cover cross-cutting verification and pull-request iterations.",
    "All estimates are most-likely (modal) values, not PERT optimistic/pessimistic averages."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Java SDK for Fabric (fabric-sdk-java feature parity)",
      "activity_description": "Design the Java package layout (client, channel, gateway, identity, event), implement gRPC clients using fabric-protos, support chaincode invocation/endorsement/query, event listening, identity/CA enrollment, and write JUnit tests and a README.",
      "most_likely_effort": 25
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Python SDK for Fabric (fabric-sdk-py feature parity)",
      "activity_description": "Implement the Python equivalent of the Java SDK using grpcio, including client/channel/identity abstractions, chaincode lifecycle, event hub, and end-to-end tests, plus a usage README.",
      "most_likely_effort": 25
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Pre-built user chaincode deployment support",
      "activity_description": "Extend the peer chaincode deployment path to accept a pre-built container image (CCID image identifier), add buildx-based multi-arch image build scripts, update the Node/Go/Java/Python SDKs to pass the image reference, and document the workflow.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Enhanced VSCC failure logging and event payload",
      "activity_description": "Modify core/committer/txvalidator VSCCValidateTx to log the active policy, satisfied signers (peer+org), and missing signers/orgs at INFO level; add a structured event payload exposed through the existing failure event channel to SDK consumers; add unit tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Platform-specific binary distribution for Fabric tools",
      "activity_description": "Add cross-compilation targets (linux/amd64, linux/s390x, linux/ppc64le, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, windows/amd64) for configtxgen, cryptogen, fabric-chaintool, fabric-ca-client, peer, orderer; add a release script that packages and signs tarballs/zip; document download instructions in the README and docs site.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "CA certificate fingerprint pinning (Auth Handler)",
      "activity_description": "Implement an endorser-side Auth Handler that, when configured, fetches the channel-configured fingerprint list endpoint, compares the endorser certificate SHA-256 fingerprint, and rejects mismatches; add channel config schema updates, unit and integration tests using a mock CA, and operator documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 15
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Testing quick start documentation",
      "activity_description": "Update the ReadTheDocs testing.html page with an overview of fabric/test/ subdirectories, links to their READMEs, and a quick-start recipe for spinning up a local network; no new test tools are created.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Consolidated configuration defaults (config_defaults)",
      "activity_description": "Audit the Go source for every configurable option in peer, orderer, gossip, ledger, endorser, configtx, and CA; produce a config_defaults/ directory containing fully populated core.yaml, orderer.yaml, configtx.yaml, and fabric-ca-server-config.yaml; update sampleconfig/ deprecation notes and link from BYFN instructions and docs.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Integration testing, CI, and code review",
      "activity_description": "Run end-to-end network tests covering SDK (Java + Python), pre-built chaincode, pinned CA certs, enhanced VSCC logging, and binary download; iterate on review comments across all stories.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    }

  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 112

}
```

technical_and_design_decisions: The NodeJS SDK (fabric-sdk-node) is used as the reference for the Java and Python SDK API surface and feature parity.

Java SDK will be implemented as a thin gRPC client on top of the existing Fabric protos (orderer, peer, event, discovery), following the same lifecycle/identity/chaincode abstractions as fabric-sdk-node.

Python SDK will be implemented using the official `grpcio` library, mirroring the same abstractions; the existing python `fabric-sdk-py` is taken as the starting point to be brought to feature parity.

For U3, pre-built user chaincode is delivered as OCI/Docker images built by the chaincode owner; the peer is extended to skip the local build step when an image reference is supplied in the chaincode deployment spec.
For U3, multi-arch images (linux/amd64, linux/s390x, linux/ppc64le, linux/arm64) are built via Docker buildx and published to a registry; the deployment spec carries the image identifier.
For U4, the enhanced VSCC log/event payload is added inside the existing VSCC ValidateTx path in core/committer/txvalidator; no policy-evaluation algorithm changes are made.

For U5, Go-based tools (configtxgen, fabric-chaintool, fabric-ca-client, cryptogen, etc.) are cross-compiled via the existing Makefile; release artifacts are packaged and hosted alongside Fabric releases.

For U6, the certificate-pinning feature is implemented as an Auth Handler (per the FAB-4207 reference) that validates endorser certs against an organization-controlled fingerprint list fetched at endorsement time.

For U6, the fingerprint list is hosted at an organization-controlled HTTP endpoint configured in the channel config; an alternative key-signed in-channel fingerprint list is not pursued in this increment to keep complexity down.
For U7, testing.html is updated to link to existing READMEs in fabric/test/ rather than authoring new tests; one sample BYFN-style network is referenced.

For U8, a `config_defaults/` directory is created at the repo root containing core.yaml, orderer.yaml, configtx.yaml, and related files with all options populated using the current code defaults; sampleconfig/ is deprecated.
assumptions: One work-day equals 8 hours of focused development by a single senior Go/JS/Java/Python developer familiar with Hyperledger Fabric internals.
The two SDKs (Java, Python) are built largely in parallel by the same developer (sequenced, not staffed) so the estimate reflects wall-clock effort of one person.
No new consensus, ordering, or state-DB features are required; existing Fabric binary protocol is reused.
CI/CD and release infrastructure for binary distribution (U5) already exists; the work is limited to wiring up cross-compilation and publishing.
Docker Hub or a similar OCI registry is available and acceptable for distributing pre-built chaincode images (U3).
The certificate-pinning implementation (U6) follows the Auth Handler approach; no changes to the gossip or orderer layers are required.
Documentation work for U7 and U8 is limited to consolidating existing content and adding links/headers; no large new tutorials are written.
An additional 10% effort is included as an 'integration testing & code review' line to cover cross-cutting verification and pull-request iterations.
All estimates are most-likely (modal) values, not PERT optimistic/pessimistic averages.
